text:
**Refined prompt:** Enumerate every HTTP route in this NestJS RealWorld API that is reachable without a JWT, answering as a security reviewer, citing the `configure()` middleware bindings and controller decorators file:line, and flagging any route that is public but shouldn't be. · Assumptions: "our endpoints" = the routes in `src/` under the `/api` prefix; "without logging in" = no `AuthMiddleware` on that path+method.

**Ten routes are public, and one of them — `DELETE /api/users/:slug` — deletes any user account by email with no token at all.** Auth is opt-in per route via `AuthMiddleware` in each module's `configure()`; anything not listed there is unauthenticated.

### Public (no token required)

| Route | Why it's public |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/` | `app.controller.ts:6`; `AppController` is in `app.module.ts:19` which has no `configure()` |
| `POST /api/users` | `user.controller.ts:32` — not in `user.module.ts:20` |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `user.controller.ts:43` — not in `user.module.ts:20` |
| **`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** | `user.controller.ts:37` — **not** in `user.module.ts:20` |
| `GET /api/articles` | `article.controller.ts:24` — not in `article.module.ts:24-31` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `article.controller.ts:38` — not listed |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `article.controller.ts:43` — not listed |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `profile.controller.ts:18` — `profile.module.ts:22` only guards `profiles/:username/follow` |
| `GET /api/tags` | `tag.controller.ts:17`; `tag.module.ts:17-18` — `configure()` is empty |
| `GET /docs` | `main.ts:18` — Swagger UI, mounted outside the `api` prefix |

### The one that matters

```ts
// src/user/user.controller.ts:37
@Delete('users/:slug')
async delete(@Param() params) {
  return await this.userService.delete(params.slug);
}
```
```ts
// src/user/user.service.ts:83
async delete(email: string): Promise<DeleteResult> {
  return await this.userRepository.delete({ email: email});
}
```

`:slug` is passed straight through as an **email**. `user.module.ts:20` applies `AuthMiddleware` to `GET /user` and `PUT /user` only — this path is not in the list. So `DELETE /api/users/victim@example.com` from any unauthenticated client deletes that account. No token check, no ownership check, no confirmation. This route isn't part of the RealWorld spec.

### Guarded, for contrast

`GET/PUT /api/user` (`user.module.ts:20`), the eight article routes at `article.module.ts:24-31`, and `profiles/:username/follow` for all methods (`profile.module.ts:22`).

Two caveats on those: the middleware only proves *who* you are, never *what* you may touch — `PUT /api/articles/:slug` (`article.controller.ts:60`) and `DELETE /api/articles/:slug` (`article.controller.ts:69`) don't even read the caller's id, so any logged-in user edits or deletes anyone's article. And `jwt.verify` at `auth.middleware.ts:17` is unwrapped, so a malformed token throws a 500 rather than a 401 — that's LESSONS.md #79, still open.

**What I did not read:** the `test/` directory, `src/shared/`, and the article/profile services. I verified route registration from the four `*.module.ts` files, the four controllers, `main.ts`, and `user.service.ts`; I did not run the app to confirm at runtime.

The ownership gaps and this delete route are already on `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`. Want me to draft the fix for `DELETE /api/users/:slug` — guard it and compare the caller against the target?
